answer: One concrete defense is a per-identity stake that goes to the verifier pool whenever an agent fails attestation. An attacker can still spin up many keys, but every clone must lock real funds at the reef of entry before it earns a single vote, and peers grade each claim blind. Cheap copies fail at that inlet: a fake agent bounces off once, loses its stake, and the pool grows. To reach a profitable zenith the swindler must fund thousands of keys, pay grading costs, and absorb each burn, which makes the attack cost more than the reward it can extract.
